To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) Lysolipids and fatty acids are more soluble in the gel-phase bilayer, and (2) their mixtures are more soluble in gel-phase bilayer than in liquid-phase bilayer.
solute induced perturbations to the bilayer structure increase solubility of the solute and solutes with similar molecular structures have similar effects on the bilayer.

the solubilities of lysolipid, fatty acid and their mixtures are bilayer concentration dependent, bilayer phase dependent and bilayer solubilization of solute is enhanced by the presence of other solutes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermodynamic properties of solutes in aqueous lipid systems.
the thermodynamics of solute partitioning between water and bilayer.
solute induced perturbation in the lipid bilayer, and the effects of this perturbation on bilayer permeability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bilayer partition coefficient of the solutes increases with increasing solute mole fraction, and that this increase is larger for the solutes in the gel phase bilayers.
the partition coefficients of the solutes are bilayer phase, concentration, and composition dependent.
the bilayer partition coefficient of the solute is greater when it is in the form of a mixture with other solute(s) than when it is in pure form.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

solute induced enhancement of transmembrane permeabilities is due to solute induced bilayers perturbations, which are composition dependent and are greater in bilayers in the gel phase than in those in the liquid phase.

the bilayer solubilities of LPPC and/or PA, or mixtures thereof, increase with solute concentration and/or composition in the bilayer phase, and this increase is greater for the gel phase than for the liquid phase.

solute induced bilayers are more permeable to water soluble solutes than the bilayers in absence of the solutes, and that solutes induce synergism toward enhanced permeability in the bilayer gel phase but not in the liquid phase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the solute composition of a lipid bilayer is a more relevant factor in determining solute induced changes in bilayer properties than the solute concentration.
the solute induced bilamellar perturbation is a key factor in solute partitioning into lipid bilayers.
solute induced bilayers perturbations are concentration dependent and that the solute induced bilayert perturbations in the gel phase are more than those in the liquid phase.
